title: From Tripods to Bipods Reducing the Queue Number of Planar Graphs Costs Just One Leg

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text contains a literal citation placeholder '?' in the reference list: "[7, 10, 14, 18, ?, 24, 27, 29, 30]". A published paper should not contain an unresolved placeholder in a citation list.

It states: "In particular, the weak dual graph of an outerplane graph is a tree." This is false in general: for an outerplane graph that is connected but not 2-connected, the weak dual can be a forest. For example, two triangles sharing only a cut vertex have a weak dual with two isolated vertices.

The proof defines layers L_0,...,L_d but sets P = (p1,...,pd), omitting p0. It then writes "For a fixed layer i ∈ {0,...,d}, K_l ⊠ P contains ... ((v1,p_i),x)", which is undefined for i=0 because p0 is not in P. The path P should include vertices p0,...,pd.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3.2, quadrangular face iterative step after applying Lemma 3.1
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Lemma 3.1 is applied to get a triangle with colors 1,2,c where c ∉ {1,2}. In a 4-coloring, c may be 3 or 4. The proof then assumes the vertex t3 is rooted at x3, effectively assuming color 3, e.g. "t3 is part of a subtree ... rooted at a vertex p3 of x3." This is unjustified when the triangle has colors 1,2,4. The lemma should be applied to the color pair 1 and 3 if the construction needs a 1-3 connection.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3.2, quadrangular face iterative step, e2/e4 paragraph
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text contains copy-paste/index errors in the quadrangular case: it states "if there is an edge e2 = (v_{k+1}, v2), where v_{k+1} ∈ B_{x_{k+1}} and v2 ∈ B_{x3}, we also connect x_{k+1} to x2", but e2 should involve B_{x2}. Then it repeats the same formula for e4: "Similarly, if there is an edge e4 = (v_{k+1}, v2), where ... v2 ∈ B_{x3}, we also connect x_{k+1} to x2", whereas e4 should involve B_{x4} and x4, as the later discussion of new faces uses x4.

After the base case n_f = 1, the proof says "Hence, assume that n_f > 2." This skips the case n_f = 2 without argument. The intended induction step should be for n_f > 1 (or n_f ≥ 2), since faces can be added one at a time starting from the base case.
